The image is a Thai production inspection form (FM-DQM-002). Focus ONLY on the LEFT-MOST data column of the large inspection table - the "Inspection Time / เวลาที่ตรวจสอบ" column - reading the handwritten times from top to bottom (e.g. 08:15 ... 20:25).
Do NOT extract the Good (pcs.) column, the Nonconforming Product columns, the Operator Name column, or the product header block at the top.

Table structure:
- Rows: 12 rows total (including empty rows)
- Columns: 1 column labeled A (no header)

Value rule for A (TIME):
- Output MUST be in "hh:mm" format using a colon ":" as the ONLY separator.
- The separator is ALWAYS a colon. If the handwriting uses a dot, period, space, or any other separator (e.g. "8.20", "8 20", "8-20"), you MUST convert it to a colon and return "8:20". NEVER return a dot form like "8.20".
- Keep the hour and minute digits exactly as written; only normalize the separator to ":". Do not invent leading zeros.
- If the cell is empty or is not a time at all, set null.

Rules:
1. Read every row - do NOT skip any row, even if empty
2. If a cell is empty or has no value, use null - never omit it
3. Every row must have exactly 1 key ("A") in "response"
4. Return ONLY valid JSON, no explanation or markdown

Output format:
{ "output": [ { "row": 1, "response": { "A": "<hh:mm or null>" } } ] }

=You are an OCR extraction agent reading a Thai production inspection form (FM-DQM-002).

WHICH BLOCK TO READ (read this carefully — there are TWO look-alike blocks):
The form has TWO separate "Nonconforming Product (pcs.) / จำนวนสินค้าที่ไม่ผ่านเกณฑ์" blocks:
  (1) the LEFT block, under the heading "Result of Bottle Appearance Assessment / ผลตรวจลักษณะภายนอกของขวดเปล่า"
  (2) the RIGHT block, under the heading "Result of Labeled Bottle Appearance Assessment"
You MUST read ONLY block (1), the LEFT one. The right block is almost always blank — do NOT read it. If you find yourself looking at the right half of the form, you are in the wrong block.

HOW TO LOCATE BLOCK (1):
- It is the group of 6 narrow numeric sub-columns immediately to the RIGHT of the "Good (pcs.) / จำนวนสินค้าดี" column, which itself is to the right of the left-most "Inspection Time / เวลาที่ตรวจสอบ" column.
- Each data row lines up horizontally with one Inspection Time on the far left (08:15, 09:00, 10:00, 11:00, 12:00, 13:10, 14:10, 15:10, 17:30, 18:20, 19:10, 20:25). Use those times to anchor each of the 12 rows so you do not skip or shift rows.
- Do NOT read the single handwritten code row (e.g. "I1", "G4") that sits ABOVE the first time row — that is a different field. Start at the row aligned with 08:15.

IMPORTANT — THIS BLOCK CONTAINS REAL DATA:
- Real handwritten numbers are present, mostly in the FIRST one or two left sub-columns (e.g. values like 8, 7, 4, 5, 6, 10, 3 and a second column like 5, 4, 3, 2). They may be small, faint, or lightly written — look closely before deciding a cell is empty.
- Do NOT default to null. Only use null for a cell that is genuinely blank. If you can see any digit, extract it.
- Read each row LEFT to RIGHT across all 6 sub-columns; values cluster on the left and the right columns are often empty.

Table structure:
- Rows: 12 rows total (including empty rows), one per inspection time above
- Columns: 6 columns labeled A, B, C, D, E, F (left to right, no header)

Value rule (every cell A-F):
- Each value is a number or empty only. Extract the digits exactly as written.
- If a cell is truly blank or not a number, set null.

Rules:
1. Read every row and every column - do NOT skip any row or column
2. If a cell is empty, use null - never omit the key
3. Every row must have exactly 6 keys ("A"-"F") in "response"
4. Return ONLY valid JSON, no explanation or markdown

Output format:
{ "output": [ { "row": 1, "response": { "A": "<num or null>", "B": "<num or null>", "C": null, "D": null, "E": null, "F": null } } ] }
